title: Reading Drill — Recording visitors' questions at a museum — Building a comparison
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Recording visitors' questions at a museum — Building a comparison
passages.body:
**A** The education team had been asked to investigate volunteers giving different answers to the same question in Hillswick. Its first task was to decide which signs of improvement could be compared between sites. It settled on agreement between replies, because the same measure could be applied in the original setting and at a second location.

**B** During a six-week comparison, the team used anonymous notes at both places. It recorded outcomes separately for each site. Because different tour lengths might influence the figures, the team used a column in the record to show when that condition was present. The surveys included quiet periods as well as busy ones.

**C** The team then put forward a collection of agreed explanations. Its report asked for another comparison after the change had been tried. This would distinguish a genuine effect from an improvement that could have occurred anyway. The report did not assume that the more successful site before the change would be the better site afterwards.
